channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Charlamagne Tha God on Netflix Deal, Midterm Elections, Mental Health
item.description: Charlamagne Tha God joins Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to talk about the world of podcasting, the "Breakfast Club" partnership on Netflix, midterm elections and much more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump: Putin To Release Diesel Into Global Market
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL) says President Trump’s deal with Russia to release diesel supplies is a “desperate political move” designed to help Republicans ahead of the midterms and argues he cares more about his party’s political outcome than addressing the cost of living. Robert Post, professor and former dean at Yale Law School, says allowing the Trump administration to decide which members of the press can access the White House could “deform the press coverage of the president” and leave the public without complete coverage. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Will Likely Cut US Long Bond Sales Next Month, Says Citi
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is likely to reduce the auction sizes for long-dated government bonds — and could even cancel sales of 20-year debt altogether, according to Citigroup Inc.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie

item.title: DOJ Scrutinizes Binance Compliance With 2023 Settlement Deal
item.description: The US Justice Department is scrutinizing whether Binance Holdings Ltd. breached a landmark settlement with the US government, as authorities probe activity on the platform for potential Iran sanctions violations.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm

item.title: Post Says White House Press Limits Could ‘Deform’ Coverage
item.description: Robert Post, professor and former dean at Yale Law School, says allowing the Trump administration to decide which members of the press can access the White House could “deform the press coverage of the president” and leave the public without complete coverage. Post says the broader conflict between the administration and the courts is a difficult one because courts rely on the executive branch’s good-faith compliance to enforce their orders. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Wasserman Schultz: Russia Diesel Deal Is ‘Desperate’
item.description: Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL) says President Trump’s deal with Russia to release diesel supplies is a “desperate political move” designed to help Republicans ahead of the midterms and argues he cares more about his party’s political outcome than addressing the cost of living. Rep. Wasserman Schultz says Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan for the public execution of Nidal Hasan a “sickening, horrific display,” questioning how children could be prevented from seeing it. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Gearing Up for Earnings (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Wall Street traders betting on another solid corporate earnings season sent stocks higher despite lingering concerns about still-elevated energy prices and bond yields. Brent crude fluctuated around $104, bringing little relief to investors worried about inflationary pressures that could make the Federal Reserve raise interest rates. Corporate America is now navigating one of the strongest profit cycles in recent history, with the S&P 500 posting seven consecutive quarters of double-digit earnings growth.
On today's episode: Seth Fiegerman, Bloomberg News AI Editor Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber Robert Schiffman, Senior Tech Credit Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence Barbara Reinhard, CIO: Multi-Asset Strategies & Solutions at Voya Investment Management (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CFTC Defends Prediction Markets Turf with New ‘Swap’ Definition
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission proposed defining financial swaps to explicitly include event contracts based on sports, politics, culture and weather-related wagers as the legal fight escalates over the booming prediction markets industry.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: James Talarico Appears in Austin After 10-Day Campaign Absence
item.description: Democrat James Talarico appeared in public for the first time since late September, returning to the campaign trail as his US Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton goes down to the wire.
item.dc:creator: Julie Fine and Joe Lovinger

item.title: Americans' Living Costs Are Top of Mind as Midterms Near
item.description: Bloomberg's Lisa Abramowicz breaks down the affordability issues that form the backdrop for the Nov. 3 midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mangione Cases Are ‘Different Harms, Different Evils,’ DA Says
item.description: Luigi Mangione should still face a New York state murder trial even after he pleaded guilty to federal charges related to the fatal shooting of UnitedHealth Group Inc. executive Brian Thompson, Manhattan prosecutors said Friday.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hurtado

item.title: What the Midterm Elections Mean for Energy, Finance and AI
item.description: Congressional gridlock will help push the boundaries of executive power.
item.dc:creator: Nathan R Dean

item.title: Hochul Opts New York Into Trump’s Divisive School Choice Program
item.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul is opting her state into the Trump administration’s controversial school choice program, according to a statement released Friday.
item.dc:creator: Erin Hudson and Raga Justin

item.title: Wall Street Sees Ominous Sign in Bond Market’s Latest Selloff
item.description: Wall Street traders betting on another solid corporate earnings season sent stocks higher in the Friday trade despite lingering concerns about still-elevated energy prices and bond yields. We examine the market backdrop with Frank Monkam, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist. OpenAI is expecting to reach or exceed $70 billion in annualized revenue by the end of the year. Bloomberg's Seth Fiegerman joins for a closer look. Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber shares findings from the firm's Ctrl Tomorrow study on technology's effects on user wellbeing and productivity. Plus - Randall Williams, Bloomberg News Sports Reporter, breaks down why the NFL is asking the Supreme Court to let states regulate prediction markets. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Putin to Supply US With Diesel Ahead of Midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump is working with Vladimir Putin to release Russian diesel supplies into global markets, a move that upends years of sanctions as the White House seeks ways to tame soaring fuel prices ahead of the US midterm election.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey, Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Will Kubzansky and Dina Khrennikova

item.title: Judge Blocks DOJ’s ‘Dragnet’ Probe of Voter Fraud Nationwide
item.description: A US judge blocked a key component of the Justice Department’s efforts under the Trump administration to obtain state voter records as part of a nationwide probe into alleged election fraud by non-US citizens.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: Iran Guards Ability to Build Missiles as Trump Eases Attacks
item.description: Iran has managed to preserve its missile and drone factories despite months of US and Israeli bombing, officials familiar with the matter said, allowing it to replenish its arsenals while President Donald Trump holds off on strikes ahead of the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Gerry Doyle, Alberto Nardelli and Alex Wickham

item.title: Trump Names Katie Zacharia as White House Press Secretary
item.description: President Donald Trump said he has appointed conservative commentator and Truth Social communications advisor Katie Zacharia as his new press secretary.
item.dc:creator: Mario Parker, Catherine Lucey and Jeff Mason

item.title: Trump Officials Clash With Mamdani Over ICE Shooting in NYC
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended the shooting of a man by an immigration officer in New York City and pushed back on calls from Mayor Zohran Mamdani and other officials to end immigration enforcement in the city.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller and Bob Van Voris

item.title: New Delhi Deploys Heavy Security Ahead of Voter-Roll Protest
item.description: From mass detentions to liquor-store closures, authorities in New Delhi are leaving little to chance as they prepare for a weekend of protests over a contentious revision of India’s voter rolls.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Roy and Sudhi Ranjan Sen
